question: What will be the average daily mean temperature in Toronto over the 7 days ending October 13, 2026, in degrees Celsius?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the mean of the daily mean 2-metre air temperatures from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-13 at latitude 43.65, longitude -79.38 (Toronto), from the ERA5 reanalysis as served by the Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com), in degrees Celsius.
research:
I couldn't find anything that settles or nearly settles this question. The forecast window (Oct 7 to 13) starts 3 to 4 weeks after today, which is beyond reliable day-to-day forecasting. Over 2015-2025, the same 7-day window in this ERA5 series averaged about **13.7 °C**, with a typical spread of about 2.4 °C and a range of 10.3 to 18.3 °C. Seasonal outlooks lean somewhat warm.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-15: I queried the Open-Meteo archive API (ERA5) for 43.65, -79.38 in Toronto local time. It already has daily mean values through 2026-09-15 (19.0 °C). Early-September daily means were 16.7 to 22.5 °C. [Open-Meteo archive](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=43.65&longitude=-79.38&start_date=2026-09-01&end_date=2026-09-15&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=America/Toronto)
- I used the America/Toronto timezone. If resolution uses UTC days, the result could differ slightly.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-09-15: Nothing has happened that settles the question. No data exists yet for the window.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center ENSO discussion keeps an "El Niño Advisory" in place. A news report on it says El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event through northern fall and winter 2026-27. [CPC Sep 2026](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_disc_sep2026/ensodisc.shtml), [elmundo.sv](https://diario.elmundo.sv/nacionales/noaa-eleva-al-75-la-probabilidad-de-que-el-fenomeno-de-el-nino-alcance-un-record-historico-a-finales-de-2026)
- Around September 2026 (I couldn't confirm the exact date): The Weather Network's Ontario fall forecast says fall as a whole leans above seasonal, linked to El Niño. But it says "we may actually run surprisingly close to seasonal for a large chunk of mid-September through mid-October," which covers the question window. [TWN](https://www.theweathernetwork.com/en/news/weather/seasonal/ontario-2026-fall-forecast)
- 2026-08-13: CPC said there was a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño this fall and winter. [CPC Aug 2026](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_disc_aug2026/ensodisc.shtml)
- The Old Farmer's Almanac calls for October near or slightly below normal, about 11 °C for southern Ontario. This is a low-reliability source. [Almanac](https://www.almanac.com/weather/longrange/region/ca/3)

## 4. Base rates (Oct 7 to 13 mean, same API and point)
- 2015: 14.4
- 2016: 14.2
- 2017: 16.4
- 2018: 15.2
- 2019: 12.9
- 2020: 13.1
- 2021: 18.3
- 2022: 11.4
- 2023: 10.3
- 2024: 11.1
- 2025: 13.4

([2025 query](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=43.65&longitude=-79.38&start_date=2025-10-07&end_date=2025-10-13&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=America/Toronto); I pulled the other years the same way.)

- Over the 11 years the mean is about 13.7 °C, the standard deviation about 2.4 °C, and the median 13.4 °C. The last four years (2022 to 2025) ran cooler, averaging about 11.6 °C, but no clear long-term trend shows over this short sample.
- Within a single week, daily means swing widely, often 8 to 22 °C. For example, 2018 ran from 22.0 down to 7.0 °C. One frontal passage can move the weekly mean by 2 to 3 °C.
- A blogTO piece citing Weather Network data says that in past strong El Niño falls, Toronto's October averaged 1.3 °C below normal. That piece was published on 2026-10-01, after today, so I'm only noting that this historical claim exists. Treat it with caution.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question.
- The Environment Canada (ECCC) seasonal outlook favours above-normal temperatures for southern Ontario in fall. I could only find the details in articles dated after 2026-09-15, so I've left them out.
- I couldn't access ECCC's monthly October outlook or NOAA CPC's outlooks for the week-3 to week-4 period. CPC's 3 to 4 week outlook issued around Sept 18 to 25, and its October monthly update, would be the most relevant expert guidance, but both come after the forecast closes.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late September to early October: extended-range model runs (ECMWF weeklies, CPC week 3 to 4) will begin to cover Oct 7 to 13.
- 2026-10-08: next CPC ENSO discussion.
- Oct 7 to 13: the actual weather. The main uncertainty is whether a cold front or a warm spell dominates that week.
- Around 2026-10-19: resolution. ERA5 data typically lags by about 5 days.
